land.text: Riyadh, 'seized from the control of the Emirate of Jabal Shammar' on 13 January 1902

predecessors.note: The Al Saud's earlier state, the Second Saudi State (emirate-of-nejd), ended in January 1891; this is a new state on the same dynasty and capital, under a new Cliopatria-split slug, not a continuation of the land.

land.text: the Sultanate of Nejd and the conquered Kingdom of Hejaz, merged by Ibn Saud on 8 January 1926 'into the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd', less the Idrisid Tihamah coast (a vassal from 1926, asir dossier)

successors.note: Nejd was raised to a kingdom on 29 January 1927 and the whole became the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September 1932 (Emirate of Riyadh page); both are other dossiers.

capitals.name: Riyadh
capitals.note: The Emirate of Riyadh page names no other seat; the capital of the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa (1913-1921) and of the Sultanate of Nejd (1921-1926) is not stated on the pages opened and is taken to be Riyadh.

rulers.name: Abdulaziz bin Abdul Rahman Al Saud (Ibn Saud)
rulers.title: Emir of Riyadh; Emir of Nejd and Hasa from 1913; Sultan of Nejd from 1921
rulers.note: The one ruler of the state: he took Riyadh on 13 January 1902, was 'ruler of the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa' in the Treaty of Darin (1915), 'declared himself sultan over Nejd and its dependencies' in 1921 and was crowned King of the Hejaz on 8 January 1926.

correction.text: Riyadh and its oasis, 'the city of Riyadh' captured on 13 January 1902

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1902-1905: Cliopatria has no Saudi shape between 1891 and 1905 (a 52 km2 sliver is marked wrong in emirate-of-nejd). The page gives only the city: Ibn Saud 'managed to capture the city of Riyadh on January 13, 1902' with about 40 men (Unification page); a disc of 60 km round Riyadh is a minimal reading. How far he held the oases (Kharj, Aflaj, Sudair) before 1906 is not on the pages opened.

correction.text: unchanged outline, but from April 1906 (Qassim) to 1912

keyframe_review.note: 375,513 km2 for 1905-1912: Riyadh province and the whole of Qassim. The Unification page has the Saudis win 'a decisive victory in Qasim on 13 April 1906' and fight on into 1907, so Qassim cannot be in the shape in 1905. The outline is right from 1906; 1902-1905 is the new keyframe above. (Cliopatria draws the same outline for the Second Saudi State in 1873-1876.)

453,592 km2 for 1913-1915: the 1905 outline plus al-Hasa (316 cells), taken in 1913: 'conquered al-Hasa from an Ottoman garrison which had controlled the area from 1871' (Unification) and 'Al-Hasa was conquered in 1913' (Emirate of Riyadh). Neither page gives an area for comparison.

450,631 km2 for 1916: the 1913 outline within 5 cells. The Treaty of Darin (26 December 1915) recognised Abdulaziz 'as the ruler of Najd and its dependencies under British protection' and 'attempted to define its boundaries', which the page does not describe; the outline is kept.

460,847 km2 for 1917-1919: 40 cells more than 1916, in the Hejaz border country. The Unification page has Saudi and Ikhwan forces capture al-Khurma from the Hashemites in 1918-1919 (ceasefire to 1924); the small addition is consistent with that, though the page names no other change. Unverified beyond that: page budget.

502,792 km2 for 1920-1921: 160 cells more than 1919, the Khurma and Turabah border country on the Hejaz side after the 1918-1919 fighting; Kuwait's fringe (11% of its cells) is in the outline but belongs to Kuwait. Corrected after review: the outline stops at 20.3 N, so the Asir highlands (Abha, 320 cells, about 81,000 km2 of Cliopatria's Asir shape outside the Tihamah) that 'the Saudis took control of ... in 1920' (Asir Province page) are added; the 1924 shape is the first Cliopatria Nejd outline to hold them (ledger 1920). Ha'il enters in November 1921, one year before the next shape (ledger).

correction.text: the 1920 outline and the Asir highlands (Abha) taken in 1920, for 1920 to November 1921
the 1922 outline and the Asir highlands, from November 1921 to 1923

keyframe_review.note: 898,817 km2 for 1922-1923: the 1920 outline plus the whole 1920 Jabal Shammar outline (Ha'il, al-Jawf, Wadi Sirhan) plus about 600 cells of the northern frontier lands. The page dates the fall of Ha'il to 2 November 1921 ('Jabal Shammar was completely conquered by Saudi forces'), so the outline starts in November 1921, not 1922; the northern cells (Arar, Turaif) are not described by any page (ledger, confidence 1). The 2 December 1922 line with Kuwait 'along the 29th parallel' (Emirate of Riyadh page) is not drawn. Corrected after review: the Asir highlands (320 cells) taken in 1920 (ledger) are added, because Cliopatria's 1922 outline stops at 20.3 N and drops them until 1924.

correction.text: the 1924-1925 outline without the Idrisid Tihamah coast: the Hejaz south of Taif and Mecca, the Asir highlands and the north up to the Iraqi frontier

keyframe_review.note: 1,050,193 km2 for 1924-1925. The southern Hejaz is inside the outline: Taif and Mecca (Taif 'surrendered without a major struggle'; Mecca 'fell without struggle' on 13 October 1924, Hussein abdicated on 16 October) plus Asir, Jizan and al-Bahah; Medina (9 December 1925), Yanbu and Jeddah (surrendered 19 December 1925) are not, which fits the pages, and the rest of the Kingdom of Hejaz joins by the December 1925 events. The Unification page says Asir was an Idrisid emirate 'under Saudi tutelage' until 1930/1934; the asir dossier (another group) says the highlands were taken in 1920. Corrected after review: the Tihamah coast of Cliopatria's Asir shape (57 cells, about 14,000 km2, Jizan to the Yemeni border) is taken out, because the Unification page has the Idrisid emirate of Asir 'under Saudi tutelage' to 1930/1934 and the asir dossier dates its Saudi suzerainty to 1926 (Saudi-Yemeni war (1934) page); the highlands stay in as direct land (ledger 1920). The earlier vassal_start of 1922 was deleted: that suzerainty begins after this state's end, in kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd.

correction.text: the Sultanate of Nejd of 1925 without the Idrisid Tihamah coast, and the last Kingdom of Hejaz shape: one realm in January 1926

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for January 1926 (the state's last days): the Sultanate of Nejd, now with the whole Kingdom of Hejaz after the surrender of 19 December 1925; on 8 January 1926 Ibn Saud 'merged his dominions into the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd'. Cliopatria ends the Nejd row in 1925 and keeps a separate Hejaz row. The Tihamah coast is left out as in the 1924 keyframe (added after review).

region.text: the city of Riyadh and its oasis

ledger.note: 13 January 1902: Ibn Saud takes Riyadh and the Al Saud have a state again. Page: he 'managed to capture the city of Riyadh on January 13, 1902'; 'The state was formed after Saudi forces seized Riyadh from the control of the Emirate of Jabal Shammar'. The Unification page: about 40 men, a night raid, the Rashidi governor Ibn Ajlan.

region.text: Riyadh province beyond the city, and the fringes, in Cliopatria's 1905 outline; page silent

ledger.note: 1905: the rest of Najd between Riyadh and Qassim is Saudi. The Unification page dates only Riyadh (January 1902) and Qassim (13 April 1906); how Ibn Saud took the oases between (Kharj, Aflaj, Sudair) is not on the pages, and Cliopatria's 1905 shape holds them. Bridge at confidence 1. Re-checked for this repair on the Battle of Rawdat Muhanna page: 'It occurred on 12 April 1906, in Muhanna's Gardens in Qassim region' and the victory 'ended the Ottoman presence in Nejd and Qassim by the end of October 1906'; the page does not mention Sudair, Kharj or Aflaj and gives no year for the Najd between Riyadh and Qassim, so the bridge stays at confidence 1. (The Unification page's 13 April 1906 and this page's 12 April differ by a day; the ledger keeps April.)

13 April 1906: Qassim passes to the Saudis. Page: 'decisive victory in Qasim on 13 April 1906', with more fighting into 1907. The year and the place are the page's; that the whole province changed hands is the reading. Jabal Shammar's Abdulaziz bin Mitaib was killed at Rawdat Muhanna in the same year (Jabal Shammar page).

1913: the Emirate of Riyadh becomes the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa. Page: 'The Emirate of Nejd and Hasa (1913-1921) was formed after Saudi forces took al-Hasa from the Ottoman garrison'. Same state, same colour.

1913: Ibn Saud takes al-Hasa and Qatif from the Ottomans. Page: Saudi forces 'conquered al-Hasa from an Ottoman garrison which had controlled the area from 1871'; Qatif was integrated afterwards (Emirate of Riyadh: 'Al-Hasa was conquered in 1913').

region.text: Nejd and Hasa under British protection

ledger.note: 26 December 1915: the Treaty of Darin puts Ibn Saud under British protection. Page: the treaty 'made the lands of the House of Saud a British protectorate and attempted to define its boundaries', recognising Abdulaziz 'as the ruler of Najd and its dependencies under British protection'; 'superseded in 1927 by the Treaty of Jeddah', after this state's end, so no vassal_end is written.

region.text: al-Khurma on the Hejaz border (not in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 1918: Saudi and Ikhwan forces fight the Hashemites for al-Khurma. Page: 'Saudi and Ikhwan forces captured al-Khurma' in 1918-1919, 'A ceasefire followed, lasting until 1924'.

region.text: al-Khurma on the Hejaz border (not in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 1919: al-Khurma goes to the Saudis. The page gives the span 1918-1919 for the capture and a ceasefire after it; the outline of 1920 carries the border country.

region.text: al-Khurma on the Hejaz border (not in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 1919: ceasefire at al-Khurma, which 'lasted until 1924'.

region.text: Abha and the Asir highlands: the part of Cliopatria's Asir shape outside the Tihamah coastal plain

ledger.note: 1920: the Saudis take Abha and the Asir highlands. 'The Saudis took control of the regional capital Abha in 1920' (Asir Province page, re-read for this repair), which also has Ibn Saud 'annexing Asir and its neighboring regions after Muhammad's death' (the Idrisi emir died in 1920) and 'incorporated the rest of Asir by 1923'. The page names no month and no tribes; the highland region (Cliopatria's Asir shape without the Tihamah) is the researcher's reading and mirrors the loss in asir /ledger/7. The Tihamah coast is not taken here: the Unification page has the Idrisid emirate 'under Saudi tutelage' to 1930/1934 and the asir dossier gives its Saudi suzerainty as 1926.

1921: Abdulaziz declares himself Sultan of Nejd. Page: he 'declared himself sultan over Nejd and its dependencies' and the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa became the Sultanate of Nejd (1921-1926). Same state, same colour.

region.text: Jabal Shammar, 'completely conquered': Ha'il, al-Jawf and the north-western oases

ledger.note: 2 November 1921: Ha'il falls and Jabal Shammar is annexed. Page: 'Jabal Shammar was completely conquered by Saudi forces' on 2 November 1921 and incorporated into the Sultanate of Nejd (Jabal Shammar page: 'The Emirate surrendered to the Saudis on November 2, 1921'). Cliopatria's 1920 Jabal Shammar outline includes al-Jawf and Wadi Sirhan; the pages do not date those separately.

region.text: the northern frontier lands Cliopatria's 1922 outline adds, page silent

ledger.note: 1922: Cliopatria adds the northern frontier lands (about 600 cells beyond Ha'il and al-Jawf). The Unification page mentions only Ikhwan raids on Transjordan from 1922 to 1924 and nothing on how the north was taken; recorded as a bridge at confidence 1. Re-checked for this repair on the Ikhwan raids on Transjordan page: Ikhwan raiders 'arrived at the undemarcated borders of Transjordan in the summer of 1922' and its infobox result reads 'Transjordan retrieves Al-Jawf, Wadi Sirhan and Kaf from Sultanate of Nejd' (1922 to 1924, no separate date); the body text has no northern frontier, no Turaif and no 1922 conquest, so the gain stays a bridge at confidence 1, and the page suggests that part of this northern land went to Transjordan after 1922, which Cliopatria's 1922-1925 shape does not show.

region.text: Kuwait's territory south of the 29th parallel, 'two-thirds of Kuwait's territory', without the land that is Kuwait's own

ledger.note: 2 December 1922: the Uqair frontier with Kuwait. Page: 'On 2 December 1922, the Nejd signed an agreement with Kuwait', the border 'a straight line along the 29th parallel' (Sultanate of Nejd page, re-read); the Unification page says Ibn Saud 'persuaded Sir Percy Cox to give him two-thirds of Kuwait's territory' and Kuwait had no representative. The area lost is the page's two-thirds, not a drawn region: the region is the band south of the 29th parallel between 46.5 E and 48.5 E (the researcher's reading) less Cliopatria's State of Kuwait outline of 1973, so Kuwait's own land (28.83-29.0 N, which the kuwait dossier draws from 1923) stays Kuwaiti. The Neutral Zone is not part of the gain: the Uqair Convention 'left the zone undefined' (a 5,770 km2 zone 'between the Saudi Arabian and Kuwaiti borders', Saudi Arabian-Kuwaiti neutral zone page, partitioned by the agreement of 7 July 1965); kuwait /ledger/4 carries it as a contest from this date. Kuwait records no matching loss at Uqair (kuwait /ledger/3 is a contest_end with emirate-of-nejd): for that dossier's owner.
29 August 1924: Ibn Saud marches on Taif. Page: 'On 29 August 1924, Ibn Saud began his military campaign against Hejaz by advancing towards Taif.'

region.text: the southern Hejaz: Taif and Mecca

ledger.note: 13 October 1924: Mecca falls, after Taif. Page: Taif 'surrendered without a major struggle'; 'The city of Mecca fell without struggle' on 13 October 1924; 'On 16 October 1924, Hussein abdicated as King of the Hejaz'. Taif is undated on the page.
9 December 1925: Medina surrenders. Page: 'The city of Medina surrendered on 9 December 1925' (a note in the page gives 5 December).

region.text: the rest of the Kingdom of Hejaz: Jeddah, Yanbu and the north

ledger.note: 19 December 1925: the Kingdom of Hejaz surrenders. Page: 'On 19 December 1925, the Kingdom of Hejaz surrendered to the forces of Ibn Saud'; the Hejaz page: Yanbu 'fell 12 days later' than Medina, Jeddah was handed over in December and Saudi forces entered its gates on 8 January 1926.
23 December 1925: the Hejaz campaign ends. Page infobox: the conquest ran 'from 29 August 1924 to 23 December 1925'.

region.text: all of Ibn Saud's dominions, Nejd and the Hejaz

ledger.note: 8 January 1926: the Sultanate of Nejd is merged into the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd. Page: 'On 8 January 1926, Abdulaziz (Ibn Saud), the Sultan of Nejd, was crowned King of the Hejaz'; he 'merged his dominions into the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd'.

wars.name: Saudi-Rashidi war
wars.outcome: Saudi victory: Riyadh 1902, Qassim in 1906, Ha'il on 2 November 1921, when Jabal Shammar was 'completely conquered'.
wars.note: The Ottomans were Rashidi allies and held al-Hasa until 1913.

wars.name: Conquest of al-Hasa
wars.outcome: Saudi victory over the Ottoman garrison in 1913.

wars.name: Khurma crisis
wars.outcome: Saudi and Ikhwan forces captured al-Khurma from the Hashemites; a ceasefire lasted until 1924.

wars.name: Kuwait-Najd border clashes
wars.outcome: Sporadic clashes over Ibn Saud's claim to Kuwaiti territory; settled by the Uqair frontier of 2 December 1922.

wars.name: Saudi conquest of Hejaz
wars.outcome: Saudi victory: Taif, Mecca (13 October 1924), Medina (9 December 1925), Yanbu and Jeddah (19 December 1925); the campaign ran 29 August 1924 to 23 December 1925.

certainty.note: Desert and tribal frontiers with no survey; the Treaty of Darin (1915) 'attempted to define' the borders of the British-protected lands but the page gives no line.
The Kuwait frontier is a straight line along the 29th parallel from 2 December 1922 and is the one sharp line; the Hejaz and northern frontiers are still undefined.

sources.title: Emirate of Riyadh
sources.note: Riyadh on 13 January 1902, the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa from 1913, the Sultanate of Nejd, the 1922 Kuwait line, the Hejaz surrender on 19 December 1925 and the merger of January 1926. The infobox came through blank.

sources.title: Unification of Saudi Arabia
sources.note: Qassim on 13 April 1906, al-Hasa in 1913, Khurma 1918-1919, Asir, Ha'il on 2 November 1921, the Uqair line, the Hejaz campaign.

sources.title: Treaty of Darin
sources.note: 26 December 1915: British protectorate, recognition as ruler of Najd and its dependencies, superseded in 1927.

sources.title: Saudi conquest of Hejaz
sources.note: 29 August 1924 to 23 December 1925: Taif, Mecca, Medina, Yanbu, Jeddah, Hussein's abdication.

sources.title: Sultanate of Nejd
sources.note: The sultanate 1921-1926, the 2 December 1922 agreement with Kuwait and the 8 January 1926 merger. Its infobox was empty on the extract.

sources.title: Asir Province
sources.note: Abha taken by the Saudis in 1920; 'incorporated the rest of Asir by 1923'.

sources.title: Battle of Rawdat Muhanna
sources.note: 12 April 1906 at Muhanna's Gardens, Qassim; end of the Ottoman presence in Nejd and Qassim by October 1906. Silent on the Najd between Riyadh and Qassim.

sources.title: Ikhwan raids on Transjordan
sources.note: 1922-1924 raids; 'Transjordan retrieves Al-Jawf, Wadi Sirhan and Kaf'. Silent on how the north was taken.

sources.title: Saudi Arabian-Kuwaiti neutral zone
sources.note: Uqair Convention of 2 December 1922 'left the zone undefined' (5,770 km2); partition agreement of 7 July 1965.

notes:
New slug, split from Cliopatria's row 'Emirate of Nejd' (1824..1925): the Second Saudi State is emirate-of-nejd (1824-January 1891); this is the Third Saudi State, from the retaking of Riyadh on 13 January 1902 to the merger on 8 January 1926. It reviews Cliopatria's shapes emirate-of-nejd_1905 to _1924; the earlier shapes of the same Name show as 'no verdict' warnings here and are reviewed in emirate-of-nejd. Other groups' dossiers (asir, kingdom-of-hejaz) name emirate-of-nejd as the 1920-1925 conqueror and should read third-saudi-state.

Page budget: five pages (Emirate of Riyadh, Unification, Treaty of Darin, Saudi conquest of Hejaz, Sultanate of Nejd); the Jabal Shammar and Muhammad bin Abdullah pages opened for the neighbouring dossiers are not cited here. No page gives an infobox area (the extractor dropped the Emirate of Riyadh and Sultanate of Nejd infoboxes), so no area comparison was possible.

Unsettled: (1) how far Ibn Saud's land reached in 1902-1905 (only the city of Riyadh is on the pages); (2) the Asir highlands: settled after review as direct Saudi land from 1920 (Asir Province page: 'The Saudis took control of the regional capital Abha in 1920') with the Idrisid Tihamah coast left out as an emirate under tutelage (Unification page) whose Saudi suzerainty begins in 1926 (asir dossier), after this state's end; the Unification page gives no year for the tutelage; (3) the northern frontier lands and al-Jawf, which Cliopatria adds in 1922 but no page dates (Jabal Shammar's 1920 outline already holds al-Jawf; the Ikhwan raids page says only that raiders reached Transjordan's undemarcated border in summer 1922 and that Transjordan later 'retrieves Al-Jawf, Wadi Sirhan and Kaf'); (4) the Kuwait cession is a polygon on the 29th parallel less Kuwait's own State of Kuwait (1973) outline, because the pages give a line and 'two-thirds' but no area, and the Neutral Zone was left undefined; (5) the end year: Cliopatria's Nejd row stops in 1925, the pages date the merger to 8 January 1926, so the final keyframe is a one-year 1926 outline that the successor dossier (kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd) also draws; (6) the Treaty of Darin protectorate is the page's word, and Britain's counterpart is the slug united-kingdom, which the eu-11 split of Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Great Britain' is to create.

Region names the gazetteer lacks: al-Khurma (used as a 60 km disc at 42.0 E, 21.9 N).

Repair pass (2026-10-25, after review): added the 1920 gain of the Asir highlands from asir (Asir Province page, confidence 2) and added the highlands to the 1920 and 1922 keyframe corrections; deleted the 1922 Asir vassal_start (confidence 1, no page year; it contradicted asir's 1926) and took the Idrisid Tihamah coast out of the 1924 and 1926 keyframes and out of the successor land; wrote the Uqair gain as the polygon minus Kuwait's 1973 outline. Four more pages were opened (Asir Province, Battle of Rawdat Muhanna, Ikhwan raids on Transjordan, Saudi Arabian-Kuwaiti neutral zone), beyond the five of the first pass, because the review asked for them; the two thin items (1905 Najd, 1922 north) stay confidence-1 bridges because those pages are silent. Disagreement kept: none.
